宏福苑火災引起各界關注維修工程圍標問題。競委會今年1月曾搜查14間工程承辦商和顧問公司，涉嫌在全港17個維修工程從事圍標等行為，估計合約總值約七億港元。行動中取得的證據揭發另有圍標集團存在，競委會今日再度搜查4間承辦商，涉及28個大廈維修工程，總值約五億元，涉嫌於投標期間提交「掩護式」標書等。

The Competition Commission announced that yesterday (the 12th), it launched a second round of enforcement action in relation to a bid-rigging case involving building maintenance, searching 12 premises, including the offices of four works contractors and the residences of persons involved in the case. The projects concerned cover maintenance works at 28 housing estates and buildings, with the total contract value initially estimated at approximately HK$500 million. The maintenance projects concerned are distributed across 12 districts in Hong Kong, Kowloon and the New Territories; some contracts have yet to be awarded, while others commenced or were completed prior to the investigation.

The Competition Commission pointed out that this action is a continuation of the first round of enforcement conducted in January this year, when 14 works contractors and consultancy firms were searched, involving 17 maintenance projects with a total value of approximately HK$700 million. The Commission stated that among the evidence obtained during that operation, a suspicious telephone message exchange was discovered, indicating the possible existence of another hidden bid-rigging syndicate intending to target the maintenance works of a certain housing estate; and according to the content of the exchange, a contractor not previously under investigation is suspected of having, during the tendering period for the estate's works, approached other contractors through an intermediary to submit cover bids, but was told in reply that some contractors had already been recruited by others to participate in bid-rigging for the same project.

The Competition Commission's analysis revealed that the contractor is suspected of having engaged in anti-competitive conduct in a number of projects, including distributing to other contractors bidding price instructions colloquially known as "homework" in order to manipulate tender outcomes; such conduct is alleged to constitute bid-rigging, market sharing, price-fixing and the exchange of sensitive information, in violation of the Competition Ordinance, and enforcement action has accordingly been taken against the contractor, other contractors involved and related persons; in addition to searching the premises, the parties have also been required to produce documents and information, and to attend hearings to provide relevant information, and it is not appropriate at this stage to disclose the subjects of the investigation or the details of the case.
